rules.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels, and unlawful for a landlord to use one when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Each month of violation and each unit affected is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms (using nonpublic competitor data under 90 days old) for setting rents or occupancy levels
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. A 'coordinated pricing algorithm' uses Competitor Data (nonpublic data on other properties, less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor.
rules.exemptions: Excludes (a) products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees or occupancy rates; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; (c) products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development. The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
rules.interaction: Local ordinance. The source does not address state or other preemption.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: two published effective dates (1 March 2026 in the ordinance text; January 2026 in an August 2026 law firm alert). Flagged for human review.
rules.notes: The source states no effective date. It records only that the Council passed the ordinance to print on November 18, 2025 (first reading). The final adoption date is not stated, so adoption_date is null. Status is in force on the assumption that the ordinance took effect before the 2026-10-01 query date under either published date. Civil remedies of up to $1,000 per violation are omitted from key_value.
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal vender, otorgar una licencia de uso o proporcionar de otro modo a los arrendadores de Berkeley un algoritmo de fijación coordinada de precios que establezca o recomiende rentas o niveles de ocupación, y es ilegal que un arrendador utilice uno al fijar las rentas o los niveles de ocupación de unidades residenciales de Berkeley. Cada mes de infracción y cada unidad afectada constituye una infracción separada.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
rules.requirement: An owner who charges a screening fee must give applicants a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the state maximum fee cap, in the application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee.
rules.key_value: Must disclose the fee rights statement and the Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) maximum fee cap before collecting a screening fee
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents who charge a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process a rental application for residential property in Berkeley. | Residential rental property in the City of Berkeley where the owner charges an applicant a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process a rental application.
rules.interaction: Implements disclosure of the state cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b); the dollar cap itself is set by state law.
rules.quoted_span:
When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)
.
rules.notes: The source gives no adoption or effective date for BMC 13.78.010, so both dates are null. The source notes the URL in the rights statement is still to be provided by the City.
rules.requirement_es: Un propietario que cobre una cuota de evaluación de solicitantes debe entregar a los solicitantes una declaración clara y visible sobre los derechos relativos a la cuota de evaluación de solicitantes y una declaración del límite máximo estatal de la cuota, ya sea en la solicitud o en un aviso separado, antes de recibir la cuota.

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or to adding or replacing a roommate.
rules.key_value: Ban on non-refundable renewal and roommate-change fees charged to existing tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: Existing tenants of residential rental property in Berkeley. Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language (BMC 13.78.018). | Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents; protects existing tenants and households.
rules.exemptions: Tenant screening fees permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 are not disallowed, including for a new or additional roommate seeking to be added to an existing lease.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.notes: The source gives no adoption or effective date for BMC 13.78.016, so both dates are null. Lease provisions that violate chapter 13.78 are unenforceable under BMC 13.78.018.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden cobrar a los inquilinos actuales una cuota no reembolsable para renovar un arrendamiento, incluidas las cuotas vinculadas a la salida de un compañero de cuarto o a la incorporación o sustitución de un compañero de cuarto.

rules.title: Berkeley just cause eviction rules as amended by Measure BB
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for nonpayment unless the rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit, bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new fixed-term lease, and tightens lease-breach evictions.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if rent debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont metro) for an equivalent-size unit
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, including government-owned or -subsidized units now required to register as fully or partially covered. | Fully covered: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses. Partially covered (just cause still applies): new construction with Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980; single-family home tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums; certain Section 202/811 and HUD-insured subsidized units. | Tenants evicted for owner move-in (Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance) or for Ellis Act withdrawal of the property from the rental market (Ellis Implementation Ordinance).
rules.exemptions: Exempt units are outside the ordinance. A unit where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord is exempt only if the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy. | Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'; owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.notes: Measure BB passed in the November 2024 election; the source states no operative date for the eviction changes. Lease-breach evictions require a material, mutually agreed term, substantial actual damage and unreasonable tenant behavior. Notices must direct tenants to the Rent Board, and copies of notices and lawsuits must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days. Owner move-in relocation assistance is adjusted for inflation annually; no amounts are given. Notice of Tenant Rights applies to tenancies started on or after 2024-12-20, which is an application date, not an effective date.
rules.requirement_es: Los inquilinos de unidades total o parcialmente cubiertas solo pueden ser desalojados por causa justa. La Medida BB prohíbe el desalojo por falta de pago a menos que la deuda de renta equivalga al menos a un mes de la Renta de Mercado Justa (Fair Market Rent) de HUD para una unidad equivalente, prohíbe el desalojo por negarse a firmar un nuevo contrato de arrendamiento de plazo fijo sustancialmente similar, y endurece los desalojos por incumplimiento del contrato de arrendamiento.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA), Rent Board Regulation 1148
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026, using the AGA set at 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase. The Order sets qualifying conditions and tenant notice requirements.
rules.key_value: 1.0% (65% of 1.5% Bay Area CPI-U, July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025)
rules.coverage_conditions: Eligible landlords of units under Berkeley rent stabilization; the AGA may not adjust rents of tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act. | Fully covered rental units under the Rent Ordinance, now including fully covered government-owned or -subsidized units (e.g. Section 8, Shelter Plus Care). Fully covered units include most multifamily units built before 1980 and single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996. | Fully covered: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually with separate leases). Not rent controlled: new construction built and issued a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980; single-family home tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums; certain HUD-subsidized units (Section 202, Section 811, and some project-based programs with HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgages). | Most units fully covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance. No increase for the rest of the year the tenancy started and one additional calendar year. Notice: 30 days for increases of 10% or less, 90 days for more than 10%.
rules.exemptions: Tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins are not adjusted by the 2026 AGA. | Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to the AGA rent ceiling. | Exempt from the ordinance: 'Golden Duplex' (owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and currently has an owner in one unit); owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives. | No AGA if registration fees are unpaid, a Rent Board order denies AGAs, there are serious repair problems or outstanding housing code violations, or interest on the security deposit is unpaid. Fixed-term leases wait until the term expires unless the lease allows the increase. Unused AGAs may be banked, and the 5% cap applies only to the AGA percentage.
rules.interaction: Operates under Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76.110A; Costa-Hawkins (state law) limits which tenancies the AGA reaches.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110(A); Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board Regulation 1148
rules.quoted_span: The 2026 AGA of 1.0% represents 65% of the increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area during the period from July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025, which was 1.5% as posted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
rules.notes: Adopted at the Board's Oct. 16, 2025 meeting (notice dated Oct. 17, 2025). Effective date taken from 'no earlier than January 1, 2026', the earliest date increases may be taken; the notice does not use the word 'effective'. The 65% of CPI formula was approved by voters in Nov. 2004.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores elegibles pueden aumentar en 1.0% los límites permanentes de renta de 2025 a partir del 1 de enero de 2026, utilizando el AGA fijado en el 65% del aumento del CPI-U del Área de la Bahía. La Orden establece las condiciones para calificar y los requisitos de notificación a los inquilinos.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or other decisions, and must give written notice and an opportunity to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: Ban on inquiring about or using criminal history in rental housing decisions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley with respect to current or prospective tenants.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.notes: Source states only that City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; no effective date stated. Official city summary page; refer to the ordinance for details.
rules.requirement_es: Los proveedores de vivienda de alquiler en Berkeley no pueden preguntar sobre antecedentes penales ni verificaciones de antecedentes penales, ni utilizarlos, en la publicidad, las solicitudes, la selección de inquilinos u otras decisiones, y deben dar aviso por escrito y la oportunidad de responder antes de tomar cualquier medida basada en antecedentes penales.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest coverage
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully and partially covered units must pay interest on tenant security deposits; exempt unit types are not subject to the requirement.
rules.key_value: Security deposit interest required for fully and partially covered units
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully covered and partially covered unit types (e.g., multifamily built before 1980, new construction after June 1980, single-family homes, most condominiums, certain subsidized units). | Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'; owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes
rules.notes: The source does not state the interest rate or the deposit cap. The last 'Yes' column is 'Security Deposit Interest'. Exact code section for interest not given in the source; citation is to the chapter generally.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de unidades total y parcialmente cubiertas deben pagar intereses sobre los depósitos de garantía de los inquilinos; los tipos de unidades exentas no están sujetos a este requisito.

rules.title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. A copy of the notice, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, must also be sent to the City's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.key_value: Notice-of-rights requirement only; no just-cause protection
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston. | All rental units and housing accommodations in Boston where a notice to quit or notice of lease nonrenewal or expiration has been served (or should have been served) on a tenant or former homeowner. | All landlords (and foreclosing owners for the City submission) planning to end a tenancy agreement in Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse. | Rental units in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; rental units in a nonprofit facility whose primary purpose is short-term (thirty or fewer days) treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rules.interaction: Notice-only ordinance; does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal under state law. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.citation: Boston Municipal Code § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.notes: Effective date from 'The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.' The ordinance was passed in October 2020 (exact day not stated). Enforcement: warning for 1st offense, then $300 per day. Source is a city FAQ summarizing the ordinance. Notice of rights requirement only; it does not limit the grounds for eviction.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador o propietario que ejecuta una hipoteca y que ponga fin a un arrendamiento debe entregar al inquilino un Aviso de Derechos y Recursos de los Inquilinos al mismo tiempo que el Notice to Quit o el aviso de no renovación del contrato de arrendamiento. También debe enviarse una copia del aviso, con un Certificado de Cumplimiento/Notificación, a la Oficina de Estabilidad de Vivienda de la Ciudad.

rules.title: H.3744 Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (not enacted)
rules.requirement: The bill would have authorized Boston to implement tenant eviction protections. It was not enacted: the last action shown is a study order on 9/9/2024.
rules.key_value: Would have authorized Boston tenant eviction protections; none in force via this bill
rules.interaction: This was a home rule petition needing state legislative approval. The bill was not enacted, so it creates no Boston eviction rule.
rules.quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
rules.notes: The source gives no bill text, so the specific eviction grounds or relocation duties are unknown. The status is inferred from the study order and the end of the session.
rules.requirement_es: El proyecto de ley habría autorizado a Boston a implementar protecciones contra el desalojo de inquilinos. No fue promulgado: la última acción indicada es una orden de estudio del 9/9/2024.

rules.title: H.3744 Boston rent stabilization home rule petition (not enacted)
rules.requirement: The bill would have authorized Boston to adopt rent stabilization, which state law otherwise bars. It was not enacted: the last action shown is a study order on 9/9/2024.
rules.key_value: Would have authorized Boston rent stabilization; no rent cap in force
rules.interaction: Massachusetts state law currently bars local rent control, so Boston needed special legislative authorization. This bill would have supplied it but was not enacted.
rules.quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.

'failed' is inferred from the end of the 2023-2024 session and the study order. The bill text and any cap formula are not in the source. The state-bar interaction comes from general background, not from the source.
rules.requirement_es: El proyecto de ley habría autorizado a Boston a adoptar la estabilización de rentas, que la ley estatal prohíbe de otro modo. No fue promulgado: la última acción indicada es una orden de estudio del 9/9/2024.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (criminal history)
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use a blanket policy denying housing to anyone with arrests or convictions and must assess applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions subject to judicial relief (expungement, sealing), juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; exclude non-conviction arrests, sealed/expunged convictions, juvenile records, and convictions over 5 years old
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. Not a general private-market rule. | Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program. | Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy. | Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, or to current criminal behavior. Conflicting federal or state criminal history requirements preempt the policy. | Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others; does not apply to current criminal behavior; conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt the policy.
rules.interaction: Federal or state law imposing a conflicting criminal history requirement preempts this policy.
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion programs, and similar non-convictions. b) Convictions that are subject to a form of judicial relief, such as expungement, sealing, and certificates for relief from disabilities. c) Juvenile records d) A conviction more than 5 years old.
rules.notes: Effective date null: the source footer shows only 'February 2017' as the policy date, with no stated effective or operative date. Official policy/guidance document, not an ordinance; applies via funding or land conditions.
rules.requirement_es: Los proveedores de vivienda cubiertos no pueden aplicar una política general que niegue vivienda a cualquier persona con arrestos o condenas, y deben evaluar a los solicitantes caso por caso. No pueden tomar en cuenta arrestos sin condena, condenas sujetas a recursos judiciales (eliminación de antecedentes, sellado), registros de menores ni condenas con más de 5 años de antigüedad.

rules.title: Boston fair housing protection for renters using rental assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters or applicants because they use rental assistance, including refusing to accept Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers.
rules.key_value: Ban on refusing rental assistance (Section 8, SSDI and veterans vouchers)
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing in the City of Boston; renters and applicants using rental assistance.
rules.interaction: The Commission enforces local, state, and federal fair housing laws. Discrimination outside Boston must be reported to the state.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Commission regulations; see also M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section 8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.
rules.notes: Secondary summary page. No effective date or specific local ordinance citation is stated, so the citation is a best reading and the effective date is null. The source lists rental assistance as a protected class, with the voucher refusal given as an example of discrimination.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Boston no pueden discriminar contra inquilinos o solicitantes por utilizar asistencia para el alquiler, incluido negarse a aceptar vales de la Sección 8, de discapacidad del seguro social o de veteranos.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term.
rules.key_value: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in a combination/conspiracy to restrain trade, or while coercing adoption of its recommended prices
rules.coverage_conditions: General antitrust law, not rental-specific. A 'common pricing algorithm' is any methodology, including a computer, software, or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. | Applies to any person using or distributing a methodology (including software) used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. It is not limited to housing; it covers rental pricing as a product or service. | A pricing algorithm is 'common' if it has two or more users and uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices or other commercial terms. Applies to any industry, not only rental housing. | Applies to any 'person' (as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702), excluding end consumers. 'Common pricing algorithm' means any methodology, including a computer, software, or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term.
rules.exemptions: 'Person' does not include the end consumer of a product or service. | Does not apply to end consumers of a product or service. | Single-firm or proprietary algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered. | End consumers of a product or service are not covered 'persons'.
rules.interaction: Statewide; Section 16729(c) says it does not impair or limit the applicability of antitrust laws. Does not address local ordinances in the source.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.notes: Approved by the Governor and filed 2025-10-06 (Chapter 338). The source gives no effective or operative date; it is treated as in force because it was enacted well before the 2026-10-01 query date. Rental housing is not mentioned in the source.
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal utilizar o distribuir un algoritmo común de fijación de precios como parte de un contrato, combinación o conspiración para restringir el comercio, o utilizar o distribuir uno mientras se coacciona a otra persona para que adopte el precio o el término comercial que recomienda.

rules.title: California application screening fee cap and conditions (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs plus the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant (CPI-adjustable). No fee may be charged when no unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must offer either first-come-first-served screening or a refund to unselected applicants, and must give an itemized receipt and a copy of any credit report.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjustable annually for CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a landlord (an owner of residential rental property) or their agent charging an applicant (including a guarantor or cosignor) to rent a residential housing unit. | Prospective tenants applying for rental units; the landlord must use a reusable screening report if the applicant provides one. | Applies to any landlord (owner of residential rental property) or agent charging an applicant (including a guarantor or cosignor) a screening fee for residential rental housing.
rules.exemptions: Not intended to preempt provisions or regulations governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs. A landlord may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1. No refund is required for an applicant denied after consideration for failing established screening criteria. The fee is not treated as an 'advance fee' or as 'security'. | Section does not preempt provisions or regulations governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs (subd. (l)). Landlords may accept a reusable screening report under Civ. Code § 1950.1.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5 (security deposits); the fee is not considered 'security' under that section. Does not preempt federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.notes: The source does not state when the $30 cap first took effect. The only date tied to the cap is the CPI adjustment 'beginning on January 1, 1998'. The section is shown as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67, Sec. 29 (AB 1170), effective 2026-01-01. The source does not show that the amendment changed the key value, so the date was not reset. The current CPI-adjusted dollar figure is not given in the source.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador solo puede cobrar una cuota de evaluación de solicitantes hasta el monto de los costos reales desembolsados más el valor razonable del tiempo dedicado, y nunca más de $30 por solicitante (ajustable según el CPI). No se puede cobrar ninguna cuota cuando no hay una unidad disponible ni se espera que lo esté pronto. El arrendador debe ofrecer evaluación por orden de llegada o un reembolso a los solicitantes no seleccionados, y debe entregar un recibo detallado y una copia de cualquier informe de crédito.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act - just cause for termination
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may terminate only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months' occupancy; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent (or waiver of final month's rent)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenant has occupied for 12 months (or 24 months if an additional adult tenant was added before an existing tenant reached 24 months, unless all tenants have 12+ months or one has 24+ months). Applies to residential real property generally, except as exempted. | Tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months, or 24 months if additional adult tenants were added to the lease before 24 months (then either all tenants have 12+ months or one has 24+ months).
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and licensed care facilities; school dormitories; shared bathroom/kitchen with owner-occupant; owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g. Single-family home) not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; mobilehome owners. | Transient/tourist hotels; certain nonprofit hospital, religious, care facilities; dormitories; shared bath/kitchen with owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property not owned by REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member (with required written notice); deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property covered by a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later local ordinance that is more protective (with a binding local finding); property is never subject to both. A less protective local ordinance adopted after 2019-09-01 is not enforced.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.notes: Effective date taken from subd. (m): 'This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.' The section as amended by AB 1529 (Stats. 2025, ch. 203) is stated to be effective 2026-01-01; it did not change the headline requirement, so the date was not reset to that. The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 by its own terms. Relocation notice must be given within the termination notice, and payment is due within 15 calendar days of service.
rules.requirement_es: Después de que un inquilino haya ocupado una unidad de manera continua y legal durante 12 meses, el propietario solo puede dar por terminado el arrendamiento por una causa justa indicada, ya sea por culpa del inquilino o sin culpa. En las terminaciones sin culpa, el propietario debe pagar un mes de renta como asistencia de reubicación o renunciar a la renta del último mes.

rules.title: Statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act), Civ. Code § 1947.12
rules.requirement: An owner may not raise the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. No more than two increments are allowed in a 12-month period for the same tenant. The owner must give notice of increases under Civ. Code § 827.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI change, max 10% (whichever is lower), per 12 months; max two increases per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property (including mobilehome park tenancies). The cap does not apply to housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome). It applies only to subsequent increases after the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains. A mobilehome tenancy is covered only for increases on or after February 18, 2021. | Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis. A unit built January 1, 2006 is covered on and after January 1, 2021. | Residential real property generally; the cap does not apply to housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome). Applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (mobilehome tenancies: on or after February 18, 2021). Section is repealed as of January 1, 2030.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school; housing under a local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property (e.g. Single-family homes, condos) whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, and where the required written exemption notice was given; a duplex in which the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence (neither unit an ADU or JADU); homeowners of a mobilehome. | Units built within the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; a two-unit property where the owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy; qualifying single-family homes and condos not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant received the required written notice; units already subject to the City's RSO. | Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable property (single-family homes, condos) if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and written notice is given; duplex where the owner occupies one unit as principal residence; mobilehome homeowners.
rules.interaction: Does not expand or limit local governments' authority to adopt rent control under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.). Housing under a stricter local rent control that limits annual increases to less than the state cap is exempt from this section, so the stricter local rule controls.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.notes: Section was repealed and re-added by SB 567 (Stats. 2023, ch. 290), effective 2024-01-01 and operative 2024-04-01 by its own terms (subd. (n)). The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 (subd. (o)). The source states the operative date of this version only. The cost-of-living index is the applicable metro CPI-U, with different April comparisons before and after August 1.
rules.requirement_es: Un propietario no puede aumentar la tasa de renta bruta en un período de 12 meses en más del 5 por ciento más el cambio porcentual local en el costo de vida, o el 10 por ciento, lo que sea menor. No se permiten más de dos aumentos en un período de 12 meses para el mismo inquilino. El propietario debe dar aviso de los aumentos conforme a Civ. Code § 827.

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council regulations)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history only within strict fair housing limits on what is sought, how it is considered, and what action is taken. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record and policies that consider arrests without convictions are prohibited.
rules.key_value: Ban on blanket criminal-record exclusions and on considering arrests without convictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing decisions by landlords in California using criminal history information.
rules.interaction: Builds on HUD 2016 disparate-impact guidance; local ordinances may add further limits.
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, § 12265 (Civil Rights Council regulations, eff. 2020-01-01)
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.conflict_note: Based on a secondary source; confirm against the official text.
rules.notes: Secondary source summary; regulation section number not given in the source, supplied from knowledge. Effective date from text: regulations 'took effect Jan. 1, 2020'.}
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores solo pueden verificar los antecedentes penales dentro de estrictos límites de vivienda justa sobre qué se solicita, cómo se considera y qué medida se toma. Están prohibidas las prohibiciones generales contra solicitantes con antecedentes penales y las políticas que consideren arrestos sin condena.

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and subsidy-tenant credit/income screening limits (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Owners may not discriminate against or harass a rental applicant or tenant because of source of income, which includes Section 8 and other housing vouchers and public assistance. Where a government rent subsidy applies, income standards must be based on the tenant's portion of rent, and applicants must be allowed to offer alternative evidence in place of credit history.
rules.key_value: Ban on source-of-income discrimination (incl. Section 8 / HUD-VASH vouchers); landlords may still ask about the level or source of income
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owners of any housing accommodation; the credit-history and income-standard rules in subd. (o) apply only where there is a government rent subsidy. | Applies to most housing providers and housing-related services covered by FEHA, including landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies. | Applies to most housing providers and tenant screening companies covered by FEHA. | Landlords subject to FEHA; applies to government housing subsidy programs such as the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. | Applicants with a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8. | Owners of housing accommodations in California; the subsidy-specific rules apply where there is a government rent subsidy. | Owners of housing accommodations and others in real-estate-related transactions; the credit-history and income-standard rules in subd. (o) apply only where there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Inquiring about the level or source of income is not discrimination; landlords may still verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity. | Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (per the FAQ); the source does not say whether this applies to source of income specifically. | Landlords may still inquire about the level or source of income, verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity. | Asking about the level or source of income is not discrimination (subd. (p)(2)). Landlords may still request employment verification, landlord references and identity verification (subd. (o)(2)).
rules.interaction: Statewide floor; this excerpt does not address local source-of-income ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.notes: Effective date is from the source's amendment note (Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, SB 267, eff. Jan. 1, 2024), which added the subsidy-tenant credit-history alternative-evidence rule and the HUD-VASH voucher language. The source does not state when the source-of-income ban was first added, so the date reflects the amendment.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden discriminar ni acosar a un solicitante o inquilino por su fuente de ingresos, que incluye la Sección 8 y otros vales de vivienda y asistencia pública. Cuando se aplique un subsidio gubernamental de renta, los estándares de ingresos deben basarse en la parte de la renta que paga el inquilino, y debe permitirse a los solicitantes ofrecer pruebas alternativas en lugar del historial de crédito.

rules.title: California residential security deposit cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security in excess of one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, and may not label any deposit 'nonrefundable'.
rules.key_value: Maximum deposit of 1 month's rent (2 months' rent for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. The two-month cap applies if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent. | The two-month cap applies to landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, where ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC in which all members are natural persons. Last month's rent counts as part of the deposit; first month's rent does not. | Residential rental agreements where the property is used as the tenant's dwelling. The 2-month cap applies only if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer. The two-month small-landlord cap does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. The cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. | The cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. The 2-month small-landlord cap does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member. Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule. The source does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.notes: Section last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective 2026-01-01; that amendment did not change the cap. Subdivision (c)(6) gives only an application date (security collected before July 1, 2024 is not covered), which is not an effective date. Photograph duties: tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025 (g)(1); return photographs from April 1, 2025 (g)(2). Service-member higher-deposit rules from April 1, 2025.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede exigir ni recibir una garantía superior a un mes de renta, además de la renta del primer mes. El arrendador debe devolver el depósito con un estado de cuenta detallado dentro de los 21 días calendario posteriores a que el inquilino desocupe la unidad, y no puede calificar ningún depósito como 'no reembolsable'.

rules.title: Cambridge policy order initiating ban on algorithmic rent-setting services
rules.requirement: The City Council unanimously passed a policy order starting steps toward banning residential property managers from contracting with companies that use algorithmic or AI-driven models to recommend rents. The city manager is to draft policy options or ordinance language for the council later this term; no ordinance has been enacted.
rules.key_value: Proposed ban on algorithmic/AI rent-recommendation services (not yet law)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential property management companies in Cambridge (described as large or corporate owners/managers).
rules.interaction: Related Massachusetts House and Senate bills on the same practice are pending at the state level; no preemption is discussed.
rules.citation: Cambridge City Council policy order (June 2026), directing city manager to draft ordinance language; no ordinance cited
rules.quoted_span: City council also unanimously passed a policy order initiating steps to ban residential property management companies from contracting companies that use algorithmic and AI-driven models to recommend what they should charge for rent.
rules.conflict_note: Based on a secondary source; confirm against the official text.
rules.notes: Secondary news source. A policy order only directs staff to draft options; it is not an enacted ordinance, so status is pending. The article says the council acted 'on Monday' (about 2026-06-22) but gives no date, so adoption_date is null. No effective date stated.
rules.requirement_es: El Concejo Municipal aprobó por unanimidad una orden de política que inicia los pasos hacia la prohibición de que los administradores de propiedades residenciales contraten con empresas que utilicen modelos algorítmicos o impulsados por IA para recomendar rentas. El administrador de la ciudad debe preparar opciones de política o texto de ordenanza para el concejo más adelante durante este período; no se ha promulgado ninguna ordenanza.

rules.title: Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge M.C. ch. 8.71)
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords and management companies must give tenants the city's rights-and-resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (e.g., Notice to Quit or Summary Process). The ordinance does not limit the grounds for eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice-of-rights requirement only; no just-cause protection
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental agreements, including a single residential dwelling unit and tenants at will; Guide required at lease signing or first month's rent tender for new tenancies, and when termination steps are taken; not required at each renewal.
rules.exemptions: Rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, or in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term assistance, treatment or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse; Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, Sec. 4.60.
rules.interaction: Does not restrict eviction actions otherwise allowed by state law; it is a notice requirement layered on state eviction procedure.
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).
rules.notes: Web page summary of the ordinance; no adoption or effective date stated in the source (page posted 10/14/2020, last modified 3/17/2025, which are not effective dates). Violation fine of $300 per day omitted from key value. Notice of rights requirement only; it does not limit the grounds for eviction.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios, arrendadores y empresas administradoras deben entregar a los inquilinos la Guía de derechos y recursos de la ciudad al inicio del arrendamiento y cuando se tomen medidas legales para dar por terminado un arrendamiento (por ejemplo, un Notice to Quit o un Summary Process). La ordenanza no limita las causas de desalojo.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source-of-income protection (incl. Section 8)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting based on source of income, which includes Section 8 and public benefits. Tenant selection standards must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants, and may be based on ability to pay rent and ability to care for the apartment and respect others' rights.
rules.key_value: Source of income (including Section 8 and public benefits) is a protected category in housing
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing transactions in Cambridge, including viewing or renting an apartment and terms and conditions of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.citation: Cambridge Municipal Code ch. 14.04 (Fair Housing Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span:
The protected categories under the Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance and the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance are the following:
Disability – Defined consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) – a physical or mental impairment which substantially limits one or more major life activities
Race
Color
National Origin or Ancestry
Family Status
Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
rules.notes: Secondary summary on the Commission's webpage; the ordinance text itself is not in the source. No effective date stated. Civil fines of up to $300 per violation are noted on the source but are not the key value.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden discriminar al alquilar con base en la fuente de ingresos, lo que incluye la Sección 8 y los beneficios públicos. Los criterios de selección de inquilinos deben ser razonables y aplicarse de manera igual y uniforme a todos los solicitantes, y pueden basarse en la capacidad de pagar la renta y la capacidad de cuidar el apartamento y respetar los derechos de los demás.

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords of residential dwelling units in Hoboken may not price-fix using algorithmic pricing, meaning software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that use nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-fixing using nonpublic competitor information
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential dwelling unit, defined as any primary residence, in the City of Hoboken. Nonpublic competitor information is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. | Any residential dwelling unit, defined as any primary residence, in the City of Hoboken. 'Nonpublic competitor information' is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. | All residential rental units in Hoboken.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit. | Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from 'residential dwelling unit'. | Medical, long-term care, or detention facilities.
rules.interaction: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect. The source does not address the FAIR Act.
rules.source_url: https://ecode360.com/HO0741 (Hoboken Code ch. 158, PDF download dated 2026-10-03)
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption: from 1 July 2027 the NJ FAIR Act may preempt the Hoboken and Jersey City algorithmic rent ordinances. Flagged for human review; not decided here.
rules.notes: Month of adoption; Adopted 7-9-2025 by Ord. No. B-781. Enforcement is by the Division of Housing or an aggrieved private citizen in Municipal Court. 158 (Ord. B-781); it is no longer pending. No Hoboken address should show a pending algorithmic rule.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de unidades de vivienda residenciales en Hoboken no pueden fijar precios mediante fijación algorítmica de precios, es decir, software, algoritmos o plataformas de intercambio de datos que utilicen información no pública de competidores para coordinar, recomendar o implementar rentas, condiciones del contrato de arrendamiento o niveles de ocupación entre arrendadores competidores.

rules.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
rules.requirement: Residential landlords raising rent by more than 10% year over year on a lease renewal must give the existing tenant specified disclosures before the increase takes effect. These are an itemization of the costs, a statement on whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the tenant's right to take legal action, and Division of Housing contact information.
rules.key_value: Disclosures required for renewal rent increases of more than 10% (no cap on the increase itself)
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords increasing rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant, year over year | All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% year over year upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant.
rules.interaction: This is a disclosure rule, not a rent cap. It also requires a statement on whether a rent algorithm was used, which links it to the algorithmic rent-fixing ban in § 158-2.
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants either in the lease upon renewal (must be clearly indicated on the first page) or on a form provided by the Hoboken Division of Housing prior to the increase being implemented:
rules.notes: Month of adoption; Classified under rent increase limits as an increase-notice requirement, although it sets no cap. Penalty (fine up to $1,000 per incident) omitted from key_value.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores residenciales que aumenten la renta en más del 10% año con año en la renovación de un contrato de arrendamiento deben entregar al inquilino actual ciertas divulgaciones específicas antes de que el aumento entre en vigor. Estas son un desglose detallado de los costos, una declaración sobre si se utilizó un algoritmo de rentas, un aviso del derecho del inquilino a emprender acciones legales y la información de contacto de la División de Vivienda.

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Control: annual rent increase cap (§ 155-5)
rules.requirement: At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not impose an increase greater than the lesser of 5% or the CPI change over the lease term. Only one such cost-of-living increase is allowed in any 12-month period. Landlords must give 30 days' written notice with reasons, include a certificate of substantial compliance, and show proof of prior rent paid.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 5% or CPI change; one increase per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units as defined in § 155-1 (housing space rented or offered for rent), except those exempt under § 155-2. Rents are controlled at the October 1, 1985 base rent. | Housing space in dwellings to which Chapter 155 applies (applicability and exemptions are defined elsewhere in the chapter, not in the source). Rents are controlled at the base rent received as of October 1, 1985 (§ 155-4).
rules.exemptions: Motels and hotels; newly constructed dwellings on first rental only (must be registered before first rental); industrial and commercial property; school-owned student housing; government-owned housing; buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984 (first rental only); multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 for the lesser of mortgage amortization or 30 years (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1). Condo/co-op owner-occupant initial rental decontrol (§ 155-37).
rules.interaction: Chapter is preempted during any period when a governmental agency regulates the rent under contract and its authority supersedes the City's (§ 155-2.1). Landlord rent-registration and proof-of-previous-rent requirements apply (§§ 155-1.1, 155-30).
rules.capture_url: https://ecode360.com/HO0741 (Hoboken Code ch. 155 Rent Control, PDF download dated 2026-10-03)
rules.quoted_span:
At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord
     may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage
     difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination
     of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
rules.notes: Section history shows 'Amended 2-1-2023 by Ord. No. B-532'. The source does not say whether that amendment changed the cap, and no operative date is stated. Other terms in the chapter: vacancy decontrol allows a 25% increase on a new tenant's initial rent (§ 155-31, once per three years per unit); a Board-approved capital improvement surcharge may not raise base rent by more than 33 1/3% in 12 months (§ 155-10); tax, water/sewer and hardship surcharges are available with Board or Officer approval. The COVID moratorium (§ 155-38) ended May 7, 2022.
rules.requirement_es: Al vencer el contrato de arrendamiento o al terminar un arrendamiento periódico, el arrendador no puede imponer un aumento mayor que el menor entre el 5% o la variación del CPI durante la vigencia del contrato. Solo se permite un aumento de este tipo por costo de vida en cualquier período de 12 meses. Los arrendadores deben dar aviso por escrito con 30 días de anticipación con los motivos, incluir un certificado de cumplimiento sustancial y presentar prueba de la renta pagada previamente.

rules.title: Preventing Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market (Ord. 25-057, § 218-12)
rules.requirement: Real estate lessors, their agents and subcontractors may not subscribe to, contract with, or pay a service provider that coordinates nonpublic competitor rental information; service providers may not facilitate agreements not to compete among lessors on rental pricing, fees or other terms.
rules.key_value: Ban on contracting with algorithmic rent-setting service providers
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to real estate lessors of residential dwelling units (primary residences) in Jersey City; 'nonpublic competitor information' is less than 365 days old and not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. | Landlords/owners of multifamily rental housing in Jersey City, per the article's description. The ordinance text is not reproduced.
rules.exemptions: Owners of multiple properties for actions related exclusively to properties controlled by the same owner; licensed real estate agents operating in accordance with state regulations; residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. | Per the article, real estate agents were excluded at the sponsor's agreement; owners of multiple buildings using algorithms but not colluding were described as outside the ban. Multiple Listing Service exclusion was discussed but its outcome is unclear.
rules.interaction: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect; not addressed in the source.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise
exchange anything of value in return for the services of a Service Provider.
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption: from 1 July 2027 the NJ FAIR Act may preempt the Hoboken and Jersey City algorithmic rent ordinances. Flagged for human review; not decided here.
rules.notes: Month of adoption; Adopted on second and final reading May 21 2025; mayor approved May 22 2025. Ordinance text is internally inconsistent in section naming (Chapter 218 titled 'Multiple Dwellings' vs 'Fees and Charges'); 25-057 (Jersey City Code § 218-12). Keep the official record's citation, quote and date.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de bienes raíces, sus agentes y subcontratistas no pueden suscribirse a un proveedor de servicios que coordine información no pública de rentas de competidores, ni contratar con él ni pagarle; los proveedores de servicios no pueden facilitar acuerdos de no competir entre arrendadores sobre precios de renta, cuotas u otras condiciones.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Municipal Code Chapter 260)
rules.requirement: Jersey City regulates rent increases through its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers. Landlords must apply through the city (via the Tyler portal) for capital improvement, vacancy capital improvement and hardship rent increases.
rules.key_value: Rent control under Ch. 260; all 1-4 unit properties are exempt
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled properties are those not exempt under the ordinance; the source notes that 1-4 unit properties are exempt.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control; owners may submit a 'Rent Control Exemption Request' if they meet the criteria for one of the permitted exemptions.
rules.quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)
rules.notes: The city page states the exemption for 1 to 4 unit properties; the cap formula itself is set out in Chapter 260 of the Municipal Code.
rules.requirement_es: Jersey City regula los aumentos de renta mediante su Rent Control Ordinance (Ordenanza de Control de Rentas), que administra la Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations. Los arrendadores deben presentar solicitud ante la ciudad (a través del portal de Tyler) para aumentos de renta por mejoras de capital, mejoras de capital por vacante y dificultad económica.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate covered tenancies without just cause and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. At-fault reasons include nonpayment, uncured lease violations, nuisance or damage, and illegal use. No-fault reasons include owner or family move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, and government vacate orders.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for listed at-fault or no-fault just causes; relocation assistance owed for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first. Can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a property with only one single-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers, and some HACLA or government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: Applies to units not covered by the City's RSO, which has its own just cause rules. The JCO does not regulate rent increases; state AB 1482 may cap rent for covered units.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq. (Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.notes: The source does not state the JCO's original effective date or the relocation amounts. Related items on the source: effective March 27, 2023, no eviction for nonpayment unless the amount owed exceeds Fair Market Rent; eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days; a Notice of Right to Counsel must be posted from August 20, 2025. The LAMC citation is inferred from general knowledge, not from the source.}
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden dar por terminados los arrendamientos cubiertos sin causa justa y deben pagar asistencia de reubicación en los desalojos sin culpa del inquilino. Los motivos por culpa del inquilino incluyen falta de pago, violaciones del contrato de arrendamiento no subsanadas, molestias o daños, y uso ilegal. Los motivos sin culpa incluyen la mudanza del propietario o de familiares, la demolición o el retiro del mercado de alquiler, y las órdenes gubernamentales de desocupación.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting for a tenant not-at-fault reason must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice, and must pay relocation assistance per unit within 15 days of serving the notice. Amounts depend on eligible or qualified status, length of tenancy and income.
rules.key_value: Eligible tenant: $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified tenant: $23,150 / $27,400; one month's rent for JCO single-family dwellings owned by natural persons. Valid July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Qualified tenant: 62 or older, handicapped or disabled, or with one or more minor dependent children. Mom & Pop reduced amounts ($10,550 eligible / $21,250 qualified) apply only for owner or family occupancy evictions where the building has four or fewer rental units and other LAMC 151.30 conditions are met. | Units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance; non-RSO units remain covered by the City's Just Cause Ordinance. | Units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance where termination rests on Subdivisions 8., 10., 11., 12., 13. Or 14. Of Subsection A. Where more than one fee applies, the landlord pays the highest. | Rental units covered by LAMC ch. XV art. 1 (RSO). Coverage definitions are not in this part.
rules.exemptions: No relocation payment when evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager (unless a manager-tenant with free or reduced rent only), or when hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster, not by landlord negligence, require eviction. Landlord may offset accumulated rent unless the eviction is due to a government order to vacate or an order for an unpermitted dwelling. | Subsection G.4. Exceptions include a replacement resident manager in the same unit and units made unsafe by fire, flood, earthquake or similar events beyond the owner's control. Resident-manager replacement allowed where the building has an existing resident manager. Protected tenants (10+ year residents aged 62+ or disabled; terminally ill) cannot be evicted under this ground. Small-landlord relocation-fee exception as described in coverage_conditions. Residential hotels as defined in Health & Safety Code § 50519 and LAMC § 47.70 et seq. (§ 151.22).
rules.interaction: For demolition of Protected Units for new construction, lower-income households get higher amounts under the Resident Protections Ordinance (eff. 2/11/2025) and the state Housing Crisis Act. Chart B standardized payments: $115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income. The higher of state or city amounts applies.
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).
rules.notes: Effective date 2026-07-01 is the start of the current annual dollar schedule (Chart A, 'Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027'; amounts increase every July 1). The underlying relocation requirement is older. Secondary fees (Relocation Service Fee, administrative fees) are omitted. This is an official LAHD summary of the LAMC. § 151.23: A landlord withdrawing or demolishing RSO units must file a Notice of Intent to Withdraw with the Department, and the withdrawal date must be at least 120 days after delivery. Qualifying tenants who are 62 or older or disabled and have lived in the unit at least one year get an extension to one year.)
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores que desalojen por un motivo sin culpa del inquilino deben presentar ante LAHD una Declaración de Intención de Desalojar antes de entregar el aviso, y deben pagar la asistencia de reubicación por unidad dentro de los 15 días siguientes a la entrega del aviso. Los montos dependen de la condición de elegible o calificado, la duración del arrendamiento y los ingresos.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable rent increases
rules.requirement: Rent on RSO units may be increased only once every 12 months by the annual allowable rent increase percentage. Effective February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add a utilities percentage, and the extra 10% for an added dependent is no longer permitted (10% for an additional non-dependent tenant is still allowed).
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage; no utilities add-on since 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28; includes apartments, duplexes, condominiums and townhomes, ADUs and JADUs, and rooms in hotels or rooming houses occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days. Mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks are also covered. | Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); check status at zimas.lacity.org. | Rental units under the RSO; housing in structures whose first Certificate of Occupancy was issued after October 1, 1978 is exempt. One-family dwellings are exempt unless two or more dwelling units are on the same parcel (duplexes and condominiums are not excepted). The Department publishes the allowable adjustment by May 30 each year; it applies to increases effective July 1 through June 30. | Applies to rental units that were the subject of a Notice of Intent to Withdraw under § 151.23 A and are re-offered for rent or lease within five years of the notice filing or of the withdrawal. | Rental units subject to the RSO. The increase is available only after the additional tenant has lived in the unit for 30 consecutive days. | Rental units subject to the RSO. Applications must be filed within 12 months after the work is completed.
rules.exemptions: Rent amount is not regulated for condominium and townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Luxury exemption available if the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978 can be established. Rent may go to market rate after voluntary move-out, certain at-fault evictions, or a Tenant Buyout Agreement. | Non-RSO properties are not covered by this figure; the source refers them to LAHD for allowable increases. | Exempt from the RSO: certificate of occupancy first issued after October 1, 1978; luxury housing certified by the Department; hotels/motels (until more than 30 days' occupancy); certain government-owned or regulated housing; affordable housing with a recorded 55-year regulatory agreement and an exemption certificate; and others. Housing Choice Voucher units are NOT exempt. No annual increase is allowed while a Franchise Tax Board noncompliance notice, a rent reduction or Rent Escrow Account Program placement, or a related criminal conviction remains uncorrected. | Replacement units built after demolition are governed by § 151.28, which allows the owner to set the initial rent but applies the RSO, with exemptions for replacement affordable units and certain owner-occupants. | Not available if the landlord knew of the additional tenant for more than 60 days and did not give notice of the increase. Not available for dependents added to an existing tenancy. | Seismic Retrofit Work does not qualify as capital improvement, rehabilitation or primary renovation work. Exceptions apply where the unit is subject to a Franchise Tax Board noncompliance notice, a rent reduction or REAP notice, or a related criminal conviction.
rules.interaction: Citywide local rent stabilization. The state Tenant Protection Act cap does not apply to units already covered by local rent control.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. ch. XV, art. 1, § 151.00 et seq. (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: two published effective dates for the new formula (2 February 2026 per LAHD; 24 January 2026 per a landlord association). Flagged for human review.
rules.notes: The allowable percentage is published annually by the Los Angeles Housing Department; the 2 February 2026 change removed the utilities add-on and the 10% add-on for an additional dependent. The rent freeze of 30 March 2020 to 31 January 2024 has ended.
rules.requirement_es: La renta de las unidades RSO solo puede aumentarse una vez cada 12 meses según el porcentaje anual permitido de aumento de renta. A partir del 2 de febrero de 2026, los arrendadores ya no pueden agregar un porcentaje por servicios públicos, y ya no se permite el 10% adicional por un dependiente agregado (sigue permitido el 10% por un inquilino adicional que no sea dependiente).

rules.title: LAMC Sec. 45.67 Prohibited Activities (source-of-income discrimination)
rules.requirement: Landlords and others offering or listing housing may not refuse to rent, renew, or terminate a tenancy, apply different terms, or advertise preferences based on a person's source of income.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in renting, terms, and advertising
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person offering for rent, renting, or listing any housing accommodation in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for any person offering for rent, renting, or listing any housing accommodation to do or attempt to do any of the following:
